title: Common Fractions: Equivalent Fractions, Simplest Form and Comparing
seo_title: Grade 6 Common Fractions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Count forwards and backwards in fractions; compare and order common fractions, including specifically tenths and hundredths; recognise and use equivalent forms of common fractions with 1-digit or 2-digit denominators (fractions where one denominator is a multiple of another).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 common fractions worksheets: equivalent fractions, simplest form, comparing, ordering and mixed numbers. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Simplest form: divide by the HCF.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Equivalent fractions: multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number.
  • Simplest form: divide both by their HCF. 1824 = 34 (÷ 6).
  • To compare, give the fractions a common denominator.
  • Improper fraction to mixed number: divide. 175 = 3 25.

Examples

Example

Compare 56 and 79

common denominator 18

15 and 14

Answer: 56 is bigger

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Bigger denominator, bigger fractionTwelfths are smaller than sixths.
Dividing one numberDivide the top and bottom.
Comparing numeratorsUse a common denominator first.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about fractions?
faq.a: Compare and order common fractions, including tenths and hundredths, recognise and use equivalent forms, and write fractions in simplest form.

faq.q: What is the simplest form of 12/16?

faq.a: No, it is an improper fraction; 1 3/4 is the mixed number.

faq.q: How do I find a common denominator?
faq.a: Use the LCM of the denominators.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
13 = ?6
items.e: The bottom bar has 6 equal parts, so each third of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 1 third becomes 1 × 2 = 2 sixths. So 13 = 26.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
34 = ?12
items.e: The bottom bar has 12 equal parts, so each quarter of the top bar is split into 3 parts. 3 quarters become 3 × 3 = 9 twelfths. So 34 = 912.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
25 = ?10
items.e: The bottom bar has 10 equal parts, so each fifth of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 2 fifths become 2 × 2 = 4 tenths. So 25 = 410.

items.q: 23 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 4 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 = 812.

items.q: 45 = ?20
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 4 = 20. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16. So 45 = 1620.

items.q: 34 = 15?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 3 × 5 = 15. Multiply the denominator by 5 too: 4 × 5 = 20. So 34 = 1520.

items.q: 23 = 10?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 5 = 10. Multiply the denominator by 5 too: 3 × 5 = 15. So 23 = 1015.

items.q: 68 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 2. Write 68 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 4 groups and 3 of them are shaded, so 68 = 34. This is the same as dividing 6 and 8 by 2.

items.q: 812 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 4. Write 812 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 3 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 812 = 23. This is the same as dividing 8 and 12 by 4.

items.q: Write 1012 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 10 and 12 is 2. Divide both numbers by 2: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So 1012 = 56.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. Count the shaded parts in all the bars: 7. So 74 is shaded. The denominator is 4 (parts in one whole), not 8 (parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. Count the shaded parts in all the bars: 5. So 53 is shaded. The denominator is 3 (parts in one whole), not 6 (parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 6 equal parts, so each part is 16. Count the shaded parts in all the bars: 11. So 116 is shaded. The denominator is 6 (parts in one whole), not 12 (parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. Count the shaded parts in all the bars: 13. So 135 is shaded. The denominator is 5 (parts in one whole), not 15 (parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 8 equal parts, so each part is 18. Count the shaded parts in all the bars: 19. So 198 is shaded. The denominator is 8 (parts in one whole), not 24 (parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole cut into 2 equal parts, so each part is 12. Count the shaded parts in all the bars: 5. So 52 is shaded. The denominator is 2 (parts in one whole), not 6 (parts in all the bars).

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 4 equal parts. 9 parts are shaded, so the amount is 94. Use the parts in one circle (4) as the denominator.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 3 equal parts. 7 parts are shaded, so the amount is 73. Use the parts in one circle (3) as the denominator.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 6 equal parts. 13 parts are shaded, so the amount is 136. Use the parts in one circle (6) as the denominator.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. What improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole cut into 8 equal parts. 11 parts are shaded, so the amount is 118. Use the parts in one circle (8) as the denominator.

items.q: 410 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 2. Write 410 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 5 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 410 = 25. This is the same as dividing 4 and 10 by 2.

items.q: 69 of the bar is shaded. The thick lines split it into groups of 3. Write 69 in its simplest form.
items.e: There are 3 groups and 2 of them are shaded, so 69 = 23. This is the same as dividing 6 and 9 by 3.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 18 and 24?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, and the highest is 6.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 12 and 30?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, and the highest is 6.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 16 and 40?
items.e: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The common factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, and the highest is 8.

items.q: What is the highest common factor of 27 and 36?
items.e: Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The common factors are 1, 3, 9, and the highest is 9.

items.q: Write 1520 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 15 and 20 is 5. Divide both numbers by 5: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 20 ÷ 5 = 4. So 1520 = 34. 3 and 4 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 1025 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 10 and 25 is 5. Divide both numbers by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 25 ÷ 5 = 5. So 1025 = 25. 2 and 5 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified.

items.q: Write 2012 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 20 and 12 is 4. Divide both numbers by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 2012 = 53. 5 and 3 have no common factor except 1, so it is fully simplified. (It is still more than 1, so the numerator stays bigger than the denominator.)

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 5 and 8 have no common factor except 1, so 58 is in its simplest form. The others can be simplified: 69 = 23 (÷ 3); 410 = 25 (÷ 2); 912 = 34 (÷ 3).

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 7 and 12 have no common factor except 1, so 712 is in its simplest form. The others can be simplified: 814 = 47 (÷ 2); 1015 = 23 (÷ 5); 39 = 13 (÷ 3).

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 4 and 6?
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, … Multiples of 6: 6, 12, … The first number in both lists is 12. 4 × 6 = 24 is a common multiple too, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 6 and 8?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, … Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, … The first number in both lists is 24. 6 × 8 = 48 is a common multiple too, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 3 and 5?
items.e: Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, … Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, … The first number in both lists is 15.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple of 9 and 12?
items.e: Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, … Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, … The first number in both lists is 36. 9 × 12 = 108 is a common multiple too, but it is not the lowest.

items.q: 35 = ?20
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. So 35 = 1220.

items.q: Write 23 and 34 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 212 and 312
912 and 812
612 and 1212
812 and 912
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12, so use 12 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 23 = 812 (× 4); 34 = 912 (× 3). Answer: 812 and 912.

items.q: Write 12 and 35 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 210 and 1510
510 and 610
910 and 810
110 and 310
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 2 and 5 is 10, so use 10 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 12 = 510 (× 5); 35 = 610 (× 2). Answer: 510 and 610.

items.q: Write 34 and 56 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 612 and 1512
1012 and 912
912 and 1012
312 and 512
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12, so use 12 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 34 = 912 (× 3); 56 = 1012 (× 2). Answer: 912 and 1012.

items.q: Write 13 and 512 as fractions with the lowest common denominator.
c: 112 and 2012
112 and 512
412 and 512
1012 and 512
items.e: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 12 is 12, so use 12 as the denominator. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 13 = 412 (× 4); 512 stays 512. Answer: 412 and 512.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 1 23?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. Count 1 whole, then 2 more marks. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 14?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. Count 2 wholes, then 1 more mark. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 75?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 75 = 1 25: go to 1, then 2 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 116?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 116 = 1 56: go to 1, then 5 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 24: 34 = 1824, 58 = 1524, 23 = 1624, 712 = 1424. The greatest is 1824, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Write them all with the denominator 36: 56 = 3036, 79 = 2836, 34 = 2736, 23 = 2436. The smallest is 2436, so the answer is 23.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All four are between 1 and 2. Look at how much each one is short of 2: 74 = 1 34 (14 short), 1 23 (13 short), 95 = 1 45 (15 short), 1 58 (38 short). The smallest gap is 15, so 95 is the greatest.

items.q: Which fraction is between 12 and 34?
items.e: In eighths: 12 = 48 and 34 = 68. 58 is between them. 78 and 45 are more than 34, and 38 is less than 12.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
23, 56, 712
c: 712, 56, 23
56, 23, 712
712, 23, 56
23, 56, 712
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 23 = 812, 56 = 1012, 712 = 712. So the order is 712, 23, 56.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 2 14 = 2712, 73 = 2812, 2 16 = 2612, 52 = 3012. The smallest is 2612, so the answer is 2 16.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
34, 23, 12
c: 34, 23, 12
34, 12, 23
12, 23, 34
23, 34, 12
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 34 = 912, 23 = 812, 12 = 612. So the order is 12, 23, 34.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
25, 13, 12
c: 13, 25, 12
12, 13, 25
25, 13, 12
13, 12, 25
items.e: Use the common denominator 30: 25 = 1230, 13 = 1030, 12 = 1530. So the order is 13, 25, 12.

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
56, 34, 78
c: 78, 56, 34
56, 78, 34
34, 56, 78
56, 34, 78
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 56 = 2024, 34 = 1824, 78 = 2124. So the order is 78, 56, 34.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
38, 14, 13
c: 38, 13, 14
14, 13, 38
38, 14, 13
13, 14, 38
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 38 = 924, 14 = 624, 13 = 824. So the order is 14, 13, 38.

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
45, 710, 34
c: 45, 34, 710
34, 45, 710
710, 45, 34
710, 34, 45
items.e: Use the common denominator 20: 45 = 1620, 710 = 1420, 34 = 1520. So the order is 45, 34, 710.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
54, 1 13, 76
c: 54, 1 13, 76
1 13, 54, 76
54, 76, 1 13
76, 54, 1 13
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 54 = 1512, 1 13 = 1612, 76 = 1412. So the order is 76, 54, 1 13.

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
53, 1 58, 1 34
c: 1 58, 1 34, 53
1 34, 53, 1 58
1 58, 53, 1 34
53, 1 34, 1 58
items.e: Use the common denominator 24: 53 = 4024, 1 58 = 3924, 1 34 = 4224. So the order is 1 34, 53, 1 58.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
2 12, 73, 94
c: 2 12, 94, 73
73, 2 12, 94
2 12, 73, 94
94, 73, 2 12
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 2 12 = 3012, 73 = 2812, 94 = 2712. So the order is 94, 73, 2 12.

items.q:
Order from smallest to largest:
23, 12, 34, 13
c: 13, 12, 23, 34
12, 23, 13, 34
12, 13, 23, 34
34, 23, 13, 12
items.e: Use the common denominator 12: 23 = 812, 12 = 612, 34 = 912, 13 = 412. So the order is 13, 12, 23, 34.

items.q: Which mixed number is “three and two fifths”?
items.e: “Three and two fifths” has 3 wholes and the fraction 25. So it is written 3 25.

items.q: Which mixed number is “two and five eighths”?
items.e: “Two and five eighths” has 2 wholes and the fraction 58. So it is written 2 58.

items.q: Which mixed number is “four and one sixth”?
items.e: “Four and one sixth” has 4 wholes and the fraction 16. So it is written 4 16.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 3 bars are full and 1 more part is shaded in the last bar. So 103 = 3 13.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 1 bar is full and 4 more parts are shaded in the last bar. So 95 = 1 45.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full and 5 more parts are shaded in the last bar. So 176 = 2 56.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 3 bars are full and 1 more part is shaded in the last bar. So 134 = 3 14.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full and 5 more parts are shaded in the last bar. So 218 = 2 58.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole. 2 circles are full. The last circle has 3 fourths shaded. So the amount is 2 34 (= 114).

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Write the shaded amount as a mixed number.
items.e: Each circle is 1 whole. 2 circles are full. The last circle has 2 thirds shaded. So the amount is 2 23 (= 83).

items.q: Write 74 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 4 are in 7? 1 × 4 = 4, so there is 1 whole. 7 − 4 = 3 fourths left over. The denominator stays 4. So 74 = 1 34. (Not 1 37: the parts are still fourths.)

items.q: Write 236 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 6 are in 23? 3 × 6 = 18, so there are 3 wholes. 23 − 18 = 5 sixths left over. The denominator stays 6. So 236 = 3 56.

items.q: Write 318 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 8 are in 31? 3 × 8 = 24, so there are 3 wholes. 31 − 24 = 7 eighths left over. The denominator stays 8. So 318 = 3 78.

items.q: Write 2912 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 12 are in 29? 2 × 12 = 24, so there are 2 wholes. 29 − 24 = 5 twelfths left over. The denominator stays 12. So 2912 = 2 512.

items.q: Write 389 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 9 are in 38? 4 × 9 = 36, so there are 4 wholes. 38 − 36 = 2 ninths left over. The denominator stays 9. So 389 = 4 29.

items.q: Write 537 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 7 are in 53? 7 × 7 = 49, so there are 7 wholes. 53 − 49 = 4 sevenths left over. The denominator stays 7. So 537 = 7 47.

items.q: Write 4710 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many groups of 10 are in 47? 4 × 10 = 40, so there are 4 wholes. 47 − 40 = 7 tenths left over. The denominator stays 10. So 4710 = 4 710.

items.q: Write 246 as a whole number or a mixed number.
items.e: How many 6s are in 24? 4 × 6 = 24, with nothing left over. So 246 = 4 wholes.

items.q: Write 459 as a whole number or a mixed number.
items.e: How many 9s are in 45? 5 × 9 = 45, with nothing left over. So 459 = 5 wholes.

items.q: Write 2 35 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 55, so 2 wholes are 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Add the 3: 10 + 3 = 13. So 2 35 = 135.

items.q: Kabelo eats 38 of a pizza. Zinhle eats 13 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Use 24ths: 38 = 924 and 13 = 824. 9 is more than 8, so Kabelo eats more.

items.q: In Class 6A, 18 of the 30 learners bring a packed lunch. In Class 6B, 14 of the 20 learners bring a packed lunch. Which class has the greater fraction of learners with a packed lunch?
items.e: Class 6A: 1830 = 35 = 610. Class 6B: 1420 = 710. 710 is more than 610, so Class 6B. Class 6A has more learners, but a smaller fraction of them.

items.q: 24 of the 32 learners in Grade 6 went on the school trip. What fraction of the learners went? Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: The fraction is 2432. The highest common factor of 24 and 32 is 8: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 32 ÷ 8 = 4. So 34 of the learners went.

items.q: Flour comes in bags of 14 kg. How many bags make 2 34 kg?
items.e: Each whole kilogram is 4 bags, so 2 kg is 2 × 4 = 8 bags. Add 3 more bags for 34 kg: 8 + 3 = 11 bags. (2 34 = 114.)

items.q: Ruan runs 134 km. Write this distance as a mixed number.
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12 and 13 − 12 = 1. So 134 km = 3 14 km.

items.q: Four children measure their ribbons. Thandi: 56 m. Pieter: 79 m. Zanele: 34 m. Sibusiso: 23 m. Who has the longest ribbon?
items.e: Use the common denominator 36: 56 = 3036, 79 = 2836, 34 = 2736, 23 = 2436. The longest is Thandi’s.

items.q: Bottle A holds 1 14 litres of water. Bottle B holds 75 litres. Which bottle holds more?
items.e: 75 = 1 25. Compare 14 and 25 using twentieths: 520 and 820. So Bottle B holds more.

items.q: Precious says, “49 is greater than 35, because 4 is greater than 3.” Is she right?
c: Yes. Ninths are bigger than fifths
No. 49 is less than 35
items.e: You cannot compare only the numerators when the denominators are different. Use 45ths: 49 = 2045 and 35 = 2745. So 49 is less than 35.

items.q: Ethan says 3 25 = 65. What is the correct improper fraction?
items.e: Ethan multiplied 3 × 2. Instead, 3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: The Reds soccer team won 7 of their 12 matches. The Blues won 5 of their 8 matches. Which team won the greater fraction of their matches?
items.e: Use 24ths: Reds 712 = 1424, Blues 58 = 1524. 15 is more than 14, so the Blues. The Reds won more matches, but they also played more.

items.q: Which letter shows 94?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 94 = 2 14: go to 2, then 1 more mark. That is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 35?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 135 = 2 35: go to 2, then 3 more marks. That is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 73?
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. 73 = 2 13: go to 2, then 1 more mark. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 2 18?
items.e: Each whole is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. 178 = 2 18: go to 2, then 1 more mark. That is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 196?
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 196 = 3 16: go to 3, then 1 more mark. That is letter C.

items.q: Palesa says 74 = 1 37. What is the correct mixed number?
items.e: Palesa used the numerator 7 as the new denominator. The parts are still fourths. 4 fourths make 1 whole, with 3 fourths left over: 74 = 1 34.

items.q: Thabo says 3 25 = 65. What is the correct improper fraction?
items.e: Thabo multiplied 3 × 2. Instead, 3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. At a class party, learners eat 19 slices. How many pizzas do they eat?
items.e: 8 slices make 1 pizza. 2 × 8 = 16, and 19 − 16 = 3 slices are left. So 198 = 2 38 pizzas.

items.q: Liam needs 3 12 cups of flour for banana bread. He only has a 14 cup measure. How many times does he fill it?
items.e: Count in fourths. 3 cups = 3 × 4 = 12 fourths, and 12 cup = 24. 12 + 2 = 14. So 3 12 = 144.

items.q: A jug holds 2 34 ℓ of water. Each cup holds 14 ℓ. How many cups can Chloe fill?
items.e: 2 ℓ = 2 × 4 = 8 fourths. Add 3 fourths: 8 + 3 = 11. So 2 34 = 114, which is 11 cups.
